newsitem.title: UK: Britain to name food safety supremo.
newsitem.headline: Britain to name food safety supremo.

text.p: The British government, seeking to restore confidence after a series of health scares, said on Thursday it would appoint an independent food safety adviser to safeguard public health.

The move, announced by Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg, follows a crisis triggered by evidence that humans could contract mad cow disease by eating infected beef and an outbreak of E-Coli food poisoning in Scotland that has claimed 18 lives.
Hogg said the new food supremo, who will head a council of up to 20 experts, would be free to criticise ministers on issues such as food safety, quality and labelling.
"We are deliberately and consciously making a rod for our own back because we're not just giving ourselves access to advice but we're exposing ourselves to public criticism," Hogg told BBC radio.
The main opposition Labour party, which has long accused the agriculture ministry of being too close to the food industry, said the appointment did not go far enough.

"What we need is an independent food standards agency which would be a massive exercise in open government, independent of commercial interests," the party's agriculture spokesman, Gavin Strang, said.
But Hogg said the new council marked an important separation of functions, whereas a separate food ministry would have a vested interest in defending the policies that it carried out.
"Our overriding duty is, and always has been, to the consumer and this council will make sure that we discharge that duty because it is public, overt and transparent," he said.
